questions.q: What is the key difference between static and dynamic provisioning?
options: There is no real difference between the two approaches
Static provisioning uses YAML, dynamic provisioning uses only kubectl commands
Dynamic provisioning only works for emptyDir volumes
In static provisioning a PV is created by hand ahead of time; in dynamic provisioning a PVC triggers automatic creation of a matching PV via a StorageClass
questions.explain: Static provisioning requires a human (or separate automation) to pre-create the PV. Dynamic provisioning lets a PVC referencing a StorageClass trigger automatic PV creation on demand.

questions.q: What does a StorageClass object actually represent?
options: A backup policy for existing PersistentVolumes
An actual provisioned disk ready to be mounted
A namespaced request for a specific amount of storage
A template/recipe describing how and where to provision storage on demand — not real storage itself
questions.explain: A StorageClass doesn't represent actual storage. It's a named configuration (provisioner + parameters) describing how storage should be created when a PVC references it.

questions.q: In a StorageClass manifest, what does the 'provisioner' field specify?
options: The Kubernetes namespace where the StorageClass lives
The name of the PVC that will use this class
The plugin, typically a CSI driver, responsible for actually creating the underlying storage
The maximum size of any volume that can be created
questions.explain: provisioner names the plugin (often a CSI driver, like ebs.csi.aws.com) that performs the real work of creating storage when triggered by a PVC.

questions.q: Northbridge's catalog-db-pvc sets storageClassName: fast-ssd and no matching PersistentVolume exists yet. What happens?
options: The PVC waits indefinitely with no action taken
Kubernetes falls back silently to emptyDir
The fast-ssd StorageClass's provisioner automatically creates a new PV matching the request, and the PVC binds to it
The PVC fails permanently since no PV exists
questions.explain: This is dynamic provisioning in action: referencing a StorageClass by name on a PVC triggers the provisioner to create a matching PersistentVolume automatically, which then binds to the PVC.

questions.q: Why would a cloud-managed cluster prefer volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer over Immediate for a StorageClass?
options: WaitForFirstConsumer disables dynamic provisioning entirely
It delays provisioning until a Pod using the PVC is scheduled, so the disk can be created in the same availability zone as that Pod's node
Immediate mode is deprecated and no longer functions on any provider
WaitForFirstConsumer is required for ReadWriteMany volumes only
questions.explain: WaitForFirstConsumer waits until the consuming Pod is scheduled before provisioning, avoiding a zone mismatch between the disk and the node that needs to mount it — a common issue with Immediate mode on cloud providers.
